overview:
OnFrontiers occupies a unique position in the expert network industry with a dual focus on two underserved markets: frontier/emerging markets and U.S. federal government contracting. Founded in 2014 by Brian Caouette, Anne Kroijer, and Kyle Teague, the company started as a peer-to-peer knowledge marketplace focused on emerging markets before expanding into federal expertise.

The emerging markets practice covers 100+ countries across six regions: Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa, MENA, CEE & CIS, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. OnFrontiers is the official Expert Platform Partner of GPCA (Global Private Capital Association, formerly EMPEA), offering favorable rates to GPCA members investing in emerging markets.

The federal government practice maintains 17,000+ vetted subject matter experts and has partnered with Chemonics International (the largest USAID for-profit contractor, with $1.5B+ in contracts). In 2025, OnFrontiers launched a partnership with GovTribe (a GovExec platform), integrating its expert profiles directly into federal contractor tools.

The company has raised approximately $7.6 million from 12 investors including Techstars, ChemCapital (Chemonics' investment arm), Right Side Capital Management, and Black & Veatch IgniteX.

history.narrative:
Brian Caouette (CEO) co-founded OnFrontiers in 2014 with Anne Kroijer (CSO) and Kyle Teague (CTO). Caouette holds an MPA from Harvard Kennedy School in International Development and Economics, and had previously founded Farmbuilders as an Echoing Green Fellow. Kroijer co-designed the platform's knowledge marketplace approach, while Teague brought technical expertise from Georgia Tech.

OnFrontiers joined the Techstars NYC Summer 2016 accelerator, gaining early-stage investment and mentorship. The company built its emerging markets expert network through partnerships with organizations like GPCA/EMPEA. A strategic inflection came when Chemonics International, the largest USAID for-profit contractor, made a strategic investment through its subsidiary ChemCapital, expanding OnFrontiers into the federal government contracting space with a Kenya office.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Consultations (Emerging Markets)
servicesDetailed.description: 30-60 minute phone/video consultations with vetted subject matter experts covering 100+ countries across Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa, MENA, CEE & CIS, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Experts matched on recency, relevancy, and depth of knowledge, typically available within 24-48 hours.

servicesDetailed.name: Federal Government Expert Access
servicesDetailed.description: 17,000+ vetted federal subject matter experts supporting government contractors, agencies, and policy organizations. Includes key personnel sourcing, proposal support, and advisory services tailored to federal acquisition processes.

servicesDetailed.name: Enterprise Knowledge Networks
servicesDetailed.description: SaaS platform enabling organizations to build proprietary networks of internal and external experts. Makes human knowledge visible, interpretable, and accessible within an organization while connecting to OnFrontiers' broader marketplace.

servicesDetailed.name: Harness Expertise Intelligence
servicesDetailed.description: Intelligence platform providing structured access to expertise data, enabling organizations to identify knowledge gaps, track expert engagement patterns, and optimize their use of human expertise.

servicesDetailed.name: Long-term Consulting Engagements
servicesDetailed.description: Multi-month advisory relationships, document review, and consulting projects that go beyond single consultations for clients needing sustained expert input.

complianceExtended.narrative: OnFrontiers operates across two highly regulated environments: international development (requiring sensitivity to local regulations, conflict of interest, and political considerations) and U.S. federal government contracting (requiring adherence to federal acquisition regulations and security clearance protocols). The company's compliance framework is adapted for these unique requirements rather than the financial services focus typical of most expert networks.

complianceExtended.regulatoryContext: OnFrontiers' dual focus on emerging markets and federal contracting places it in a distinct compliance environment. Federal work requires adherence to FAR regulations, while development work involves USAID, World Bank, and multilateral institution standards. This differs significantly from the MNPI/securities-focused compliance typical of finance-oriented expert networks.

clientFit.narrative: OnFrontiers is uniquely positioned for organizations working in emerging/frontier markets or the U.S. federal government space. These are niche markets where traditional expert networks have limited coverage. Clients focused on developed market finance or corporate strategy will find more comprehensive options elsewhere.
